answer: A new identity enters only when an established mirror countersigns its admission with the registrar's quill, locking a $500 pearl bond for 90 days. The quill writes the signature into a ledger, and if the newcomer is caught running a duplicate, the mirror loses the bond. Forging 1,000 identities needs 1,000 mirrors risking $500 each, $500,000 in bonds at stake, while one honest agent pays nothing and enters on the word of a neighbor it knows.
